subject: Chainguard onboarding: load acceptance inventory & next steps
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@chainguard.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Chainguard onboarding: load acceptance inventory & next steps

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for picking Redwood for inference serving. Ahead of our load runs I'd like to confirm the acceptance inventory so we can hand over clean artifacts to QA and CS. Below is the proposed acceptance checklist and what we need from your side: 

Acceptance targets (proposed):
- Sustained throughput: 200 RPS for 30m steady window (90% of traffic)
- P95 latency: <= 250 ms (tokenized generation baseline)
- Tail latency (P99): <= 500 ms
- Error rate: < 0.5% (5xx/unavailable)
- Cold-start recovery: full KV-cache resync < 30s for a failed replica restart

What we will deliver to you as evidence after the run:
- Raw telemetry (per-token latency traces) and summarized CSVs
- Load script used (CSV + traffic profile) and runner config
- Canary logs and warmup traces for KV cache behavior
- Short write-up with pass/fail against each acceptance item

What we need from Chainguard: 
- Test credentials (service account + ephemeral key) for the staging endpoint (S3/secret link preferred)
- Representative request samples or a traffic profile file (histogram of seq lengths, prompt mixes)
- Preferred 2-hour window for an initial acceptance run (we propose Aug 19 08:00–10:00 PDT)

Attachments: redwood-runbook-v1.pdf (run instructions, config), example template for results.

If that all looks good I will loop in our infra on Monday to provision the reserved pool and pin the model variant for the run.

Thanks,
Grace

Grace O'Connor
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0127
[Attachment: redwood-runbook-v1.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@chainguard.com>

Date: Fri, 15 Aug 2025 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Chainguard onboarding: load acceptance inventory & next steps

Hi Grace —

Thanks for the clear checklist. We can commit to the proposed targets with a small caveat: our production seq-length distribution is slightly heavier on 512+ tokens during search workloads. I attached a traffic profile YAML that represents a 70/30 split short/long requests.

We will: 
- Upload a staging service account key to the secure bucket by EOD Monday (Aug 17)
- Provide an IP allowlist for the Redwood runner
- Block initial run to Aug 19 08:00–09:30 PDT (we prefer a 90m window for a warmup + steady stretch)

If you want us to reduce sequence length for the first smoke we can provide a trimmed profile. Otherwise run as proposed and we'll evaluate.

Regards,
Sarah Lopez
SRE Lead, Chainguard
sarah.lopez@chainguard.com
[Attachment: chainguard_traffic_profile.yml (text/x-yaml)]

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@chainguard.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 16 Aug 2025 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Chainguard onboarding: load acceptance inventory & next steps

Sarah — thanks for the profile, that's helpful. A few quick implementation notes from the runner side: 

- We'll run an initial 20m warmup with KV-cache priming (replay of top 5% prompts) before ramping to the 200 RPS steady window. Warmup reduces P99 variance.
- Proposed steady-state trial: 90 minutes at target throughput (with 10m ramps up/down at 25% increments).
- We'll enable continuous batching with a max latency budget of 100 ms to avoid batching-induced tail spikes; that keeps the p95 tighter.
- Please provide the staging endpoint + key in the secure bucket listed in your note. Also share any rate-limiting headers your infra requires so we can include them in the runner.

Attached is a first-pass load script (loadscript_v2.csv) and the runner flags we'll use. If you prefer, we can also run a short A/B with quantized model to show cost/latency tradeoffs — let me know.

Thanks,
Dev

Dev Patel
Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com
[Attachment: loadscript_v2.csv (text/csv)]
